newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian state insurer denies takeover report.
newsitem.headline: Romanian state insurer denies takeover report.

text.p: Romanian state insurer Asigurarea Romaneasca ASIROM SA on Thursday denied a media report that a prominent local businessman was acquiring a controlling stake in the company.
The independent daily Ziua said George Paunescu would sign a contract to buy 51 percent of ASIROM, the country's main insurance company, from the State Ownership Fund.
"There was neither a contract signed today at ASIROM headquarters to sell ASIROM shares nor talks on this issue," the insurer said in a statement.

ASIROM was created in 1991 after the government disbanded the communist-era ADAS insurer. It took over ADAS's life insurance assets and liabilities and until recently held the monopoly of compulsory insurance in the Balkan country.
It still controls more than half of the nascent insurance market.
Paunescu, a former foreign trade diplomat under communism has built up with his brothers the most powerful conglomerate in Romania, spanning oil to airlines.

In February Romania scrapped the communist-era practice which made insurance for individual property and passenger liability mandatory, opening the industry to competition. In practice ASIROM faces little commercial opposition. -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
